summary: The prepared base already contains upstream PR #37971, which fixes the issue-specific GLM mixed image/video offset ambiguity. A deterministic legacy-versus-current reproduction on gfx950 showed that the old generic lookup assigned all shared-token spans to both modalities, while the current implementation partitions them correctly using video boundaries. No new runtime fix was added; the unrelated open zero-padding proposal was not adopted because it lacks semantic-correctness evidence.

tests.what_was_measured: 11 focused tests passed, including mixed image/video ordering, interleaving, distinct token IDs, chunk overlap counting, and short/long embedding boundaries. Raw output: reports/j-5f70e3d76bd8/raw/focused_pytest.log

On gfx950, the legacy generic lookup assigned four spans to each modality; the current implementation assigned the two image spans only to IMAGE and the two video-frame spans only to VIDEO. Raw output: reports/j-5f70e3d76bd8/raw/gpu_mixed_offsets.log

gpu_execution.evidence: AMD Instinct MI355X, arch gfx950:sramecc+:xnack-, recorded in reports/j-5f70e3d76bd8/raw/gpu_mixed_offsets.log

remaining_limitations: GLM-5.3-Flash weights and the reported 8xH20 TP8/DP8/EP8 serving environment were unavailable; no full-model, HTTP, multi-GPU, or multi-node reproduction was claimed.

The generic _adjust_embedding_length helper still raises for a synthetically short embedding, so this verifies the reported mixed image/video trigger fix rather than universal request-level isolation for all future mismatch causes.
The assigned GPU is AMD gfx950 rather than H20; GPU execution validates tensor-based offset classification only, not GLM model accuracy.
No native source changed, so no native rebuild was applicable.
